key_insight: Point2Part reframes 3D part decomposition as a whole-shape partitioning problem: parts should be predicted jointly, without overlaps or gaps, so they fully reconstruct the original object. This makes part segmentation more consistent and usable for downstream 3D applications.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the limitation of existing 3D part decomposition methods that can produce overlapping parts or leave uncovered regions, which breaks the integrity of the original shape and reduces utility for part-level tasks.
method: Uses point prompts to guide 3D part decomposition.
Predicts all parts jointly as a unified partition of the full shape.
Enforces non-overlapping parts that collectively recover the entire object.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners working with 3D data, this provides a cleaner and more reliable way to obtain part-level representations. It is especially useful for applications that require complete, disjoint parts such as editing, manipulation, retrieval, and simulation.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of overlapping/gappy parts vs. unified partitioning

paper_title: Point2Part: Unified 3D Partitioning from Point Prompts
paper_authors: Hao-Tang Tsui, Yu-Rou Tuan, Xiaoxuan Ma, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Takaaki Shiratori
